payload.headline: Micron slips 1.59% to 798.44 on no news; stalls under resistance before earnings

summary.thesis: Micron is a grade-A, cash-rich business earning peak margins, and at 798.44 the price already assumes peak cash flow roughly holds.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold, and add closer to the 730.29–745.24 support zone. Swing: wait.
summary.act_at: Add near 745.24; reconsider or trim above 833.11

payload.happening: MU closed at 798.44, down 1.59% on the day, with no news since the last note. The price sits just under a resistance zone at 803.67–818.62 (a price area where selling has stopped rises before) and below its falling 20-day average of 843.03 and 50-day average of 947.28. The next earnings report is due on 2026-12-23.
payload.business: The business numbers are exceptional. Quarterly revenue grew 345.03% from a year earlier, up from 196.29% two quarters ago, and grew 30.81% from the previous quarter. Operating margin (profit from operations as a share of sales) reached 74.59%, up from 26.14%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 59.0B from 1.7B. The balance sheet is very safe: 38.4B in cash against 2.8B of debt, which leaves 40.6B of net cash. The main risk to the business is the margin. The filings flag that the 75% operating margin sits at the top of its 5-year range of -41% to 75%, and peaks like this usually fade. Memory chip pricing has historically moved in cycles (general knowledge). Insiders sold $14.0M outside pre-set plans, and the stock is high versus its own 5-year range. Those points affect sentiment and governance, not demand or cash. The solvency of the company is not at risk. What is at risk is how long earnings stay at this level.

worth.text: A standard discounted cash flow model (a valuation based on projected future cash) is not used, because free cash flow jumped from 1.7B to 59.0B in one year and a one-year jump can't be projected forward. The useful test is a reverse one: the current price implies starting free-cash-flow growth of only 2.4%. With zero growth from today's cash flow the value is 724.81, and with 10% growth it is 1073.53. So the price assumes today's peak cash flow roughly holds without growing much. The margin test points the same way. At 20% starting growth, a fall in operating margin to 37% gives a value of 805.56, close to today's price. Against its own history the stock looks expensive. Its price-to-sales ratio (company value per dollar of sales) of 6.8 is at the 78th percentile of its own 5-year range, and that history puts value at 322.32–833.11 with a midpoint of 490.66. Against peers it looks cheap: 6.8 times sales versus a peer median of 8.6, and 0.32 on a growth-adjusted basis. The gap between the methods comes down to one question: is this a lasting margin level or a cyclical peak? The trailing P/E (price over the last year's earnings) is 10.8, which looks low only if earnings stay where they are.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow stays near today's 59.0B instead of falling as the 74.59% operating margin fades.

bull: Revenue growth is speeding up: up 345.03% from a year earlier this quarter, versus 196.29% two quarters ago.
The price implies only 2.4% starting cash-flow growth, while 10% growth would be worth 1073.53.
The stock is cheap against peers (price-to-sales 6.8 versus a peer median of 8.6) and has 40.6B of net cash.
bear: Operating margin of 74.59% is at the top of its 5-year range (-41% to 75%), up from 26.14%, and the filings say peaks like this usually fade.
Price-to-sales is at the 78th percentile of its own 5-year history, and that history tops out at a value of 833.11.
The trend is weak: the price is below the falling 50-day average of 947.28, and insiders sold $14.0M outside pre-set plans.

levels.what: Top of the 730.29–745.24 support zone, close to the 724.81 value that assumes flat cash flow. A better place to add.
Top of the own-history valuation range. Above it the price assumes more than holding today's peak, so it is a level to reconsider or trim.
Bottom of the lower support zone (643.53–658.48, two touches). A close below it would suggest the market doubts the margins.

longterm.why: The business is A-grade with a strong balance sheet, but at 798.44 the price already assumes peak cash flow holds. Holding fits that; adding is better near 745.24.

swing.why: The price is in a sideways range, pressing into the 803.67–818.62 resistance zone, with the falling 20-day average at 843.03 above it. With an ATR (average daily trading range) of 59.79, the room to the next resistance is small for the risk. Cleaner setups would be a close above 861.1 or a test of 730.29–745.24 support that holds.

decision.timing: Options price a 9.4% move by 2026-11-20 and 21.6% by 2027-01-15, a window that includes the 2026-12-23 earnings report. Implied volatility of 71.4 is below the recent realized 105.6, so swings may run larger than options price, and big new positions before the report carry event risk.

change_mind: The 2026-12-23 report shows operating margin falling toward 37%. At that level the value is 805.56, so the margin cushion behind the hold view would be gone.
A close below 643.53, under the lower support zone, would turn the range into a downtrend and move the view toward avoid.
A close above 861.1 with the 20-day average (843.03) turning up would end the range and support a swing entry.
payload.what_changed: The price fell from 811.30 to 798.44 with no news and moved slightly closer to the add zone. Nothing in the business or valuation data changed, so the view stays hold.
